Quantum interference operator

Source: R/interference.R
interference.Rd

Applied to the whole population with probability `interference_rate`. Two variants are available:

- `"diagonal"`: quantum interference crossover (Narayanan & Moore, 1996). The amplitudes of the j-th qubit of individual i are copied from individual ((i + j - 2) mod popsize) + 1, so that each new individual is a "diagonal" combination of the whole population. Fitness is not used.

- `"amplitude"`: fitness-weighted amplitude interference. Amplitudes are first brought to a canonical form (alpha, beta >= 0, which leaves the measurement probabilities unchanged), then each qubit receives the signed sum of the amplitudes of the whole population: $$\psi_i \leftarrow \psi_i + \lambda \sum_k w_k \psi_k, \quad w_k = (f_k - \bar{f}) / \sum_k |f_k - \bar{f}|$$ Individuals above the average fitness contribute with positive sign (constructive interference), those below with negative sign (destructive interference). Amplitudes that would become negative are set to 0 (complete cancellation), and the qubit is renormalized to its original norm; if both amplitudes cancel, it is reset to the equal-probability state.

Individuals whose measured chromosome equals the best solution are left unchanged (as in rotation and mutation).

interference(
  interference_rate,
  popsize,
  chromosome,
  solution_best,
  q_alphabeta,
  genomeLength,
  interference_type = "diagonal",
  fitness = NULL,
  interference_lambda = 0.5
)
